'''Jiří (Jirka) Matoušek''' (10 March 1963 – 9 March 2015) was a [[Czech people|Czech]] [[mathematician]] working in [[computational geometry]] and [[algebraic topology]]. He was a professor at [[Charles University]] in [[Prague]] and the author of several textbooks and research monographs.

==Biography==
Matoušek was born in Prague. In 1986, he received his [[Master's degree]] at Charles University under [[Miroslav Katětov]].<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Matoušek |first=Jiří |date=1986 |title=Vlastnosti R-stromů |degree=M.Sc. |language=Czech|publisher=Charles University in Prague}}</ref> From 1986 until his death he was employed at the Department of Applied Mathematics of Charles University, holding a professor position since 2000. He was also a visiting and later full professor at [[ETH Zurich]].<ref name="rememberingJM" />

In 1996, he won the [[European Mathematical Society#Prizes|European Mathematical Society prize]]<ref>[http://www.euro-math-soc.eu/ems_prize_winners.html EMS Prize Winners] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120418072815/http://www.euro-math-soc.eu/ems_prize_winners.html |date=2012-04-18 }}.</ref> and in 2000 he won the Scientist award of the [[Learned Society of the Czech Republic]].<ref>[http://www.learned.cz/main.php?id=02.03.01.2000 2000 Awards] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090103223046/http://www.learned.cz/main.php?id=02.03.01.2000 |date=2009-01-03 }}, Learned Society of the Czech Republic.</ref> In 1998 he was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Matoušek, Jiří|chapter=Mathematical snapshots from the computational geometry landscape|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=365–375|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011593000}}</ref> He became a fellow of the Learned Society of the Czech Republic in 2005.<ref>[http://www.learned.cz/en/fellows-of-the-learned-society-of-the-czech-republic/fellows-of-the-learned-society/matousek-jiri.html Member profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160308111604/http://learned.cz/en/fellows-of-the-learned-society-of-the-czech-republic/fellows-of-the-learned-society/matousek-jiri.html |date=2016-03-08 }}, [[Learned Society of the Czech Republic]], retrieved 2015-03-10.</ref>

Matoušek's paper on computational aspects of [[algebraic topology]] won the Best Paper award at the 2012 ACM [[Symposium on Discrete Algorithms]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.siam.org/meetings/da12/paper.php |title=SIAM: Best Paper Awards |access-date=18 March 2015}}</ref>

Aside from his own academic writing, he has translated the popularization book ''Mathematics: A Very Short Introduction'' by [[Timothy Gowers]] into Czech.<ref>{{cite book|last=Gowers|first=Timothy| title=Mathematics: A Very Short Introduction|trans-title=Matematika: Průvodce pro každého|others=Translated by Jiří Matoušek| language=Czech |publisher=Dokořán|date=2006|isbn=80-7363-083-4 }}</ref> He was a supporter and signatory of the [[Cost of Knowledge]] protest.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://thecostofknowledge.com/ |quote= I've been practicing this for many years, with some exceptions (journals with few good alternatives, requests for reports from people I didn't want to disappoint). I hope this initiative will not die out.|title=The Cost Of Knowledge|access-date=18 March 2015}}</ref>

Matoušek died in 2015, aged 51.<ref name="rememberingJM">{{cite web |url= http://kam.mff.cuni.cz/Matousek-obituary.html |title= Prof. Jiří Matoušek |access-date= 2015-03-18 |author1=Jan Kratochvíl |author2=Martin Loebl |author3=Jarik Nešetřil |author4=Pavel Valtr |quote= In the name of Jiří Matoušek's colleagues and friends from Charles University }}, obituary</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mff.cuni.cz/to.en/verejnost/konalo-se/2015-03-matousek/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161012133853/http://www.mff.cuni.cz/to.en/verejnost/konalo-se/2015-03-matousek/|url-status=dead|archive-date=12 October 2016|title=Obituary of Jiří Matoušek|date=12 March 2015|website=Faculty of Mathematics and Physics, Charles University|access-date=18 March 2015}}</ref> In 2021, a lecture hall at the [[Faculty of Mathematics and Physics, Charles University]], was named after him.<ref>[https://www.mff.cuni.cz/cs/verejnost/aktuality/nejvetsi-poslucharna-matfyzu-nese-jmeno-prof-jiriho-matouska Největší posluchárna Matfyzu nese jméno prof. Jiřího Matouška], mff.cuni.cz</ref>
